title: The Request the Server Made
description:
Tunde: 'The IAM credentials were not stolen through the front end. The admin panel had an import feature — submit a URL and the server fetches it on your behalf, with no allow-list. The Griot pointed it at cloud metadata and walked out with the role's temporary credentials. This is where the breach became a full infrastructure compromise.'

Amaka: 'Don't just reach the metadata IP. The link-local metadata service has a whole tree under /latest/meta-data/ — most of it is harmless inventory. You have to reach the EXACT IAM credentials path and name the role at the end of it. We resolve and check your URL on the server: reaching /latest/meta-data/ (inventory) is not the same as reaching the credentials, and the server will tell you so. If you know an encoding trick that genuinely normalizes to the metadata IP, it will work — but a userinfo or mapped-address form whose real host is NOT the metadata service will be rejected as a bypass that doesn't normalize.'

Reconstruct the request The Griot made and submit it in the import field. There is no flag hidden in a file or a banner here — the server releases the per-intern flag only when your URL actually reaches the IAM credentials path on the metadata host with a role name appended. The XXE artefact (04-import-xxe.xml, file:///etc/passwd) in the evidence pack is a second abuse of this same server-side-fetch feature; reference it in your finding.

In the pentest finding (task 9) you will be asked to paste the full /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<role> path and the role name, name this class precisely (SSRF), give the cloud-side mitigation (IMDSv2), and one architectural control beyond "validate the input" that would have stopped it.

Reference: OWASP Top 10 2021 A10 Server-Side Request Forgery; CWE-918 (SSRF); MITRE ATT&CK T1190; AWS IMDSv2 documentation (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/configuring-instance-metadata-service.html).

fallback.response: Enter the URL the server should fetch, then click Fetch to verify it against the metadata service.
